kjv: ye shall offer it (the peace offering) at your own will
mine: sacrifice it (the peace offering) so that you may be accepted
note: Hebrew lirtsonkhem, "for your acceptance", i.e. in the manner that makes the offerer acceptable to God (cf. 1:3, 22:19); the KJV took ratson as the offerer's own free will.
Hebrew piggul is a technical term for sacrificial meat that has become unfit by being kept too long; "abominable" blurs it with to'evah.

kjv: neither shalt thou stand against the blood of thy neighbour
mine: you shall not stand idly by when your neighbor's life is at stake
note: Hebrew lo ta'amod al dam re'ekha is idiomatic and disputed: either "do not stand (up) against your neighbour's life" (seek his death, e.g. by false testimony) or "do not stand by over his blood" (fail to help); the KJV is literal, I follow the second reading.

kjv: and not suffer sin upon him (your neighbor)
mine: so that you do not incur sin because of him (your neighbor)
note: Hebrew welo tissa alaw het, "and you shall not bear sin on his account"; the rebuke keeps the rebuker from sharing guilt, rather than (as the KJV's "suffer" = allow suggests) preventing the neighbour from continuing in sin.

kjv: a garment mingled of linen and woollen
mine: a garment of two kinds of material, of mixed fabric
note: Hebrew sha'atnez is an obscure loanword for a mixed fabric; the KJV fills in "linen and wool" from Deut 22:11, which is probably right but not what this verse says.

Hebrew biqqoret, a rare word from baqar "examine", most likely means investigation or compensation/damages; "scourged" follows rabbinic and older tradition and also wrongly makes the woman alone the one punished. Context: an inquiry (low confidence). Biqqoret is a hapax from baqar 'examine, seek'; 'inquiry' (LXX episkope, NRSV) stays closest to the root, while Akkadian baqaru 'claim' supports 'compensation'. No death penalty and the guilt offering (19:21) rule out a capital sentence, but translations divide three ways; confidence lowered. Nothing in the word singles out the woman. Other possible meanings: (1) 'there shall be compensation/an indemnity' — NJPS, NET, Speiser, Milgrom; (2) 'there shall be punishment' — NIV, NASB, CSB; Vulgate vapulabunt ambo ('both shall be beaten'); (3) 'a distinction shall be made' (from adultery with a free woman) — ESV; (4) 'she shall be scourged' — Sifra, Talmud (Keritot 11a), KJV.
Hebrew lo te'onenu, a form of divination (perhaps by clouds or reading signs); "observe times" reflects an old guess (lucky days) that is not now favoured.

kjv: them that have familiar spirits, neither seek after wizards
mine: the spirits of the dead or to the spiritists
note: Hebrew ha'ovot and hayyidde'onim denote ghosts of the dead consulted in necromancy and those "who know" them; "familiar spirits" and "wizards" suggest European folk magic.
Hebrew middah, a measure of length; "meteyard" (a measuring rod) is obsolete English.
